form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Ms. Baldwin introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation

form.official-title: To improve the efficiency and reliability of rail transportation by reforming the Surface Transportation Board, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Rail Shipper Fairness Act of 2020.

subsection.text: Section 11101(a) of title 49, United States Code, is amended by inserting , as necessary for the efficient and reliable transportation based on the shipper’s reasonable service requirements, after the transportation or service.
Section 11123(b) of such title is amended by adding at the end the following:

paragraph.text: The Board may issue emergency service orders that include shipments moving under contract if such shipments are part of a regional service order issued in accordance with this section.

subsection.text: Section 11145(a) of such title is amended—

paragraph.text: in paragraph (1), by striking and at the end;
by redesignating paragraph (2) as paragraph (3); and
by inserting after paragraph (1) the following:

reports, service plans, or other documents that cover shipments moving under contract if such shipments are part of a general report, service plan, or other document that generally covers the geographic area or commodity; and

subsection.text: Section 11704 of such title is amended—

paragraph.text: in subsection (a), by inserting or subjected to inadequate or deficient service after injured;
by amending subsection (b) to read as follows:

subsection.text: A rail carrier providing transportation subject to the jurisdiction of the Board under this part is liable—

paragraph.text: for damages sustained by a person as a result of an act or omission of that carrier in violation of this part;
to a person for amounts charged to that person that exceed the applicable rate for the transportation; and
to a person for damages or equitable relief as a result of inadequate or deficient service in violation of this part.
in subsection (c), by adding at the end the following:

The Board may order a rail carrier to pay damages or to provide equitable relief, as appropriate, to a person subjected to inadequate or deficient service as a result of a violation of this part by that carrier.

subsection.text: Section 11901 of such title is amended—

paragraph.text: in subsection (a), by striking $5,000 and inserting $25,000;
in subsection (c), by striking $5,000 and inserting $25,000; and
in subsection (e), by striking $100 each place such term appears and inserting $1,000.

subsection.text: Section 10101 of title 49, United States Code, is amended—

paragraph.text: by redesignating paragraphs (14) and (15) as paragraphs (15) and (16), respectively; and
by inserting after paragraph (13) the following:
to provide for and promote the protection of the shipping public from the unreasonable exercise of market power;

subsection.text: Section 10705 of such title is amended by adding at the end the following:
Shippers may obtain rates to or from any interchange points of 2 or more rail carriers.
Section 10707 of such title is amended—

paragraph.text: in subsection (a)—

subparagraph.text: by striking In this section, market dominance means and inserting the following:

paragraph.text: effective competition only includes modes of transportation with existing and supporting infrastructure; and
market dominance means
in subsection (b)—

subparagraph.text: by inserting A rail carrier could have market dominance even in circumstances in which a shipper is served by 2 carriers. after the rate applies.; and
by striking rate or transportation and inserting rate for transportation.

subsection.text: Section 11102(c) of such title is amended to read as follows:

paragraph.text: Except as provided in paragraph (2), the Board shall require a Class I rail carrier to enter into a competitive switching agreement if a shipper or receiver, or a group of shippers or receivers, files a petition with the Board that demonstrates, to the satisfaction of the Board, that—

subparagraph.text: the facilities of the shipper or receiver for whom such switching is sought are served by rail only by a single, Class I rail carrier; and
subject to paragraph (3), there is, or can be a working interchange between—

clause.text: the Class I rail carrier serving the shipper or receiver for whom such switching is sought; and
another rail carrier within a reasonable distance of the facilities of such shipper or receiver.

paragraph.text: Competitive switching may not be imposed under this subsection if—

subparagraph.text: either rail carrier between which such switching is to be established demonstrates that the proposed switching is not feasible or is unsafe; or
the presence of reciprocal switching will unduly restrict the ability of a rail carrier to serve its own shippers.

paragraph.text: The requirement set forth in paragraph (1)(B) is satisfied if each facility of the shipper or receiver for which competitive switching is sought is—

subparagraph.text: within the boundaries of a terminal of the Class I rail carrier; or
within a 100-mile radius of an interchange between the Class I rail carrier and another carrier at which rail cars are regularly switched.

subsection.text: Section 10701(d) of title 49, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:

subparagraph.text: Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of the Rail Shipper Fairness Act of 2020, the Board shall initiate a rulemaking proceeding to develop a methodology for determining the reasonableness of challenged rail rates based on competitive rate benchmarking that predicts a competitive rate level based upon econometric models.
Rather than utilizing its existing Three-Benchmark Methodology, the Board shall develop a methodology that considers competitive markets or a proxy of such markets.

In determining the reasonableness of a challenged rate under the new benchmarking methodology developed under this paragraph, the Board shall presume that a rate above the benchmark rate level is unreasonable unless the rail carrier proves that the margin above the competitive rate benchmark is necessary to allow the rail carrier to earn adequate revenues.
Relief under the new benchmarking method shall have no monetary limit and any rate prescription set by the Board shall remain in effect not less than 5 years.
The Board’s rulemaking under this paragraph shall set a standard procedural schedule for such cases, subject to necessary adjustments in particular adjudications, which may not exceed 1 year.

subsection.text: Section 10702 of such title is amended—

paragraph.text: by inserting (a) before A rail carrier; and
by adding at the end the following:

The Board shall prohibit a rail carrier providing transportation subject to the jurisdiction of the Board under this part from increasing the challenged rate for providing such transportation to rail customers while a maximum reasonable rate case brought by such rail customers is pending before the Board.
A rail customer may file a maximum reasonable rate case with the Board after the date that is 2 years before the date on which a common carrier shipment rate is anticipated to begin.
The Board may not use cross-subsidy tests in deciding stand-alone cost cases.
The Board shall use a market-based revenue divisions methodology in deciding stand-alone cost cases.

In a stand-alone cost case, if the Board determines that the rail carrier is revenue adequate, the rail carrier shall have the burden of proof to demonstrate that the railroad carrier is charging a reasonable rate.

subsection.text: Section 10704 of such title is amended—

paragraph.text: by striking subsection (c); and
by redesignating subsection (d) as subsection (c).

subsection.text: Section 10707(d)(1)(B) of such title is amended by adding at the end the following A shipper may introduce movement-specific Uniform Rail Costing System cost calculations..

section.text: Section 10701 of title 49, United States Code, as amended by section 4(a), is further amended by adding at the end the following:

paragraph.text: A rail carrier providing transportation subject to the jurisdiction of the Board under this part may not use an index when establishing fuel surcharges.

Any fuel surcharges imposed by the rail carrier shall be directly accounted for by changes to the carrier’s actual fuel prices. The carrier’s fuel surcharge may not be greater than the amount necessary to recover the carrier’s incremental fuel cost increases.
The Board is authorized to require any rail carrier to report actual fuel prices as necessary to carry out the purposes of this subsection.
A shipper may challenge a fuel surcharge as an unreasonable practice under section 10702(2) if such charges, as applied to that shipper, exceed the carrier’s incremental fuel costs.

section.text: Section 10704(a)(3) of title 49, United States Code, is amended to read as follows:

paragraph.text: In calculating a rail carrier’s cost of capital, the Board shall multiply the value of the capital by the sum of—

subparagraph.text: the current annual yield on a 10-year United States Treasury Bond; and
a prospective market risk premium, which shall not exceed 5 percent per year.

section.header: GAO study on changes in freight railroad operating and scheduling practices

subsection.text: The Comptroller General of the United States shall conduct a study of the impact on freight rail shippers, Amtrak, commuter railroads, railroad employees, and other affected parties of changes in freight railroad operating and scheduling practices as a result of the implementation of the precision scheduled railroading model.
The study conducted pursuant to subsection (a) shall examine—

paragraph.text: the impacts of the precision scheduled railroading model on the operation of longer trains;
the safety impacts of the reduction in workforce, including occupational injury rates, impacts to inspection frequencies and repair quality, and changes in workforce demands;
the elimination or downsizing of yards, repair facilities, and other operational facilities;
increases in demurrage or accessorial charges or other costs to shippers;
capital expenditures for rail infrastructure; and
the effect of changes to dispatching practices and locations of dispatching centers on—

subparagraph.text: the on-time performance of passenger trains; and
the quality and reliability of service to freight shippers.

subsection.text: Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Comptroller General of the United States shall submit a report to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives summarizing the results of the study conducted pursuant subsection (a), including recommendations for addressing any negative impacts of precision scheduled railroading on freight shippers or passenger railroads.
